He attended [[St. Benedict's Preparatory School]] and played a [[postgraduate season]] at [[IMG Academy]]. He then played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Quiñones grew up in [[Brentwood, New York]] and started playing [[basketball]] in sixth grade. In his first two years of high school, he attended [[Brentwood High School (New York)|Brentwood High School]]. As a junior, Quiñones transferred to Upper Room Christian School in [[Dix Hills, New York]] and averaged 19.3 points per game.{{cite web|first=David|last=Cordova|title=Lester Quinones: Long Island Native Makes A Name Himself Nationally|url=https://davesjoint.net/2019/01/11/lester-quinones-long-island-native-makes-a-name-himself-nationally/|work=Dave's Joint|date=January 11, 2019|access-date=August 3, 2019}} He was named to the 2017 [[Long Island]] Basketball honor roll.{{cite web|title=2017 Basketball Honor Roll|url=http://www.longislandbasketball.com/2017HONORroll.html|website=LongIslandBasketball.com|access-date=August 3, 2019}} For his senior season, Quiñones moved to [[St. Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]]. He joined a nationally ranked basketball program and became teammates with five-star recruit [[Precious Achiuwa]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=New Jersey Tip-Off Notebook: Lester Quinones, Precious Achiuwa, Louis King, Trey Patterson Show Out|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2017/12/17/new-jersey-tip-off-day-1-notebook-lester-quinones-precious-achiuwa-louis-king-trey-patterson-show/|website=ZagsBlog.com|date=December 17, 2017|accessdate=August 3, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=Way-too-early high school basketball Top 25 for 2018-19|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/ghIaR39LT0yQxzSc4_6lpg/way-too-early-high-school-basketball-top-25-for-2018-19.htm|work=[[MaxPreps]]|date=May 17, 2018|access-date=August 3, 2019}} On January Rankings|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/NButa016SESBIK9bDDYyNA/final-2017-18-maxpreps-high-school-top-25-boys-basketball-rankings.htm|work=[[MaxPreps]]|date=April 2, 2018|access-date=August 4, 2019}} In the summer, Quiñones played for New Heights alongside Achiuwa, averaging 15.2 points and 4.7 rebounds on the [[Under Armour]] Association (UAA) circuit.{{cite web|first=Lukas|last=Harkins|title=NCAA Basketball Recruiting: Analyzing favored five for Lester Quinones|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/04/16/ncaa-basketball-recruiting-analyzing-favored-five-lester-quinones/|website=BustingBrackets.com|date=April 16, 2019|access-date=August 4, 2019}} Entering the 2018–19 season, he transferred to [[IMG Academy]], a prep school in [[Bradenton, Florida]] with a successful basketball program, joining the [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate]] team.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=Precious Achiuwa, Lester Quinones transfer to Florida powerhouses from St. Benedict's Prep|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/08/13/precious-achiuwa-lester-quinones-transfer-to-florida-powerhouses-from-st-benedicts-prep/|website=ZagsBlog.com|date=August 13, 2018|access-date=August 4, 2019}} Quiñones averaged 24 points, nine rebounds, and six assists per game, shooting 38 percent on three-pointers.{{cite web|title=Lester Quinones - 2019-20|url=https://gotigersgo.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8771&path=mbball|work=University of Memphis Athletics|access-date=August 4, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Quiñones finished his high school and postgraduate career as a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]].{{cite web|title=Lester Quinones, 2019 Shooting guard|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/lester-quinones-207267|website=Rivals.com|access-date=August 4, 2019}} On May 10, 2019, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] under head coach [[Penny Hardaway]]. He had also strongly considered playing for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].{{cite magazine|first=Alaa|last=Abdeldaiem|title=Four-Star Prospect Lester Quinones Is The Latest Star Joining Penny Hardaway In Memphis|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/05/10/lester-quinones-decision-commits-memphis|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 10, 2019|access-date=August 4, 2019}} with broken hand|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28165190/memphis-guard-lester-quinones-3-weeks-broken-hand|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 25, 2019|access-date=November 26, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Quiñones was named to the [[American Athletic Conference]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite web|title=American Athletic Conference Announces All-Conference, All-Freshman Teams|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2020/3/9/mens-basketball-american-athletic-conference-announces-all-conference-all-freshman-teams.asp|work=[[American Athletic Conference]]|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 11, 2020}} He averaged 10.7 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game.{{cite news|first=Christian|last=Fowler|title=Freshman Review: Lester Quinones|url=https://247sports.com/college/memphis/Article/Freshman-Review-Lester-Quinones-146236012/|work=247 Sports|date=April 19, 2020|access-date=September 13, 2020}} After his junior season, Quiñones announced his intentions to leave Memphis and enter the [[NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Quiñones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Golden State Warriors]] on July 5, 2022.{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Fahey|title=Warriors Sign Lester Quinones to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/lester-quinones-signed-2-way-contract-20220705|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2022|access-date=July 14, 2022}} Quiñones debuted for the Warriors' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] team in the NBA California Classic, scoring seven points, five rebounds, and two steals in a 68–86 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings vs Golden State Warriors Jul 2, 2022 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sac-vs-gsw-1322200002/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2022}} He was waived by the Warriors on October 13.{{cite tweet|author=Warriors PR|title=Warriors waive Lester Quinones and Quinndary Weatherspoon|number=1580606718542635012|user=WarriorsPR|date=October 13, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2024}} On October 15, 2022, Quiñones signed with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2022 Training Camp Roster|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2022-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022|archive-date=October 24, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221024231301/https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2022-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} On February 25, 2023, Quiñones had 42 points and 8 rebounds in a 112–119 loss to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]]. On March 2, 2023, Quiñones signed a 10-day contract with Golden State, but saw no playing time.{{cite tweet|author=Warriors PR|title=Warriors sign guard Lester Quinones to 10-Day contract|number=1631362899800371200|user=WarriorsPR|date=March 2, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023}} Ten days later, he was reacquired by Santa Cruz.{{cite web|title=2022-2023 Santa Cruz Warriors Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Santa-Cruz-Warriors/35/Transaction_History/2023|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 22, 2024}} On March 17, 2023, Quiñones signed a two-way contract with Golden State.{{cite tweet|author=Warriors PR|title=Warriors sign guard Lester Quinones to two-way contract|number=1636823556477849600|user=WarriorsPR|date=March 17, 2023|access-date=March 17, 2023}} He made his NBA debut on March 31, versus the [[San Antonio Spurs]], playing one minute and securing his first rebound.{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs vs Golden State Warriors Mar 31, 2023 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sas-vs-gsw-0022201158/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023}} On April 4, he was named the [[NBA G League Most Improved Player Award|NBA G League Most Improved Player]].{{cite web|first=Brett|last=Siegel|title=Golden State Warriors Guard Named G League Most Improved Player|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/golden_state_warriors_guard_named_g_league_most_improved_player/s1_16925_38660356|website=Yardbarker.com|date=April 4, 2023|access-date=April 4, 2023}} On July 24, 2023, Quiñones signed another two-way contract with the Warriors{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guard Lester Quinones to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-guard-lester-quinones-to-two-way-contract-20230724|website=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2023|access-date=July 25, 2023}} and on February 22, 2024, he signed a standard contract with Golden State.{{cite web|title=Warriors Convert Guard Lester Quinones to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-convert-guard-lester-quinones-to-standard-nba-contract-20240222|website=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024}} On March 3, he led the Warriors in points and minutes in a blowout loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Golden State Warriors vs Boston Celtics March 3rd, 2024 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-bos-0022300872/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2024}} ===Philadelphia 76ers / Delaware Blue Coats (2024)=== On September 26, 2024, Quiñones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Lester Quinones to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-lester-quinones-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} However, he was waived on December 3.{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Pete Nance to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-pete-nance-two-way-contract-dec-2024|website=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2024|access-date=December 3, 2024}} ===Birmingham Squadron / New Orleans Pelicans (2024–2025)=== On December 6, 2024, Quiñones was acquired by the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite web|title=SQUADRON ACQUIRE QUINONES IN TRADE WITH SANTA CRUZ WARRIORS|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/squadron-acquire-quinones-in-trade-with-santa-cruz-warriors|website=NBA.com|date=December 6, 2024|access-date=December 7, 2024}} His strong performances in the G League culminated in the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] signing him to a two-way contract on March 3, 2025.{{Cite web|title=Former Memphis basketball star Lester Quiñones signs two-way deal with Pelicans|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/2025/03/03/memphis-basketball-lester-quinones-tigers-pelicans-nba-penny-hardaway/81152467007/|access-date=April 2, 2025|website=commercialappeal.com|language=en}} He debuted with the Pelicans on March 24, helping his team secure a 112–99 victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{citation needed|date=January 2026}} In nine appearances for the Pelicans, Quiñones averaged 8.6 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 2.6 assists. On August 18, 2025, Quiñones signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web | last=Chacon | first=Aidan | title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Guard To Exhibit-10 Contract | website=Orlando Magic On SI | date=2025-08-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/magic/onsi/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-guard-to-exhibit-10-contract-01k2zd5ajrz7 | access-date=2025-12-09}} He was waived by Orlando on October 18.{{Cite web|title=Magic waive Reece Beekman, Lester Quiñones, Javonte Smart, and Phillip Wheeler|url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/rumors/2025/10/18/magic-waive-reece-beekman-lester-quinones-javonte-smart-and-phillip-wheeler/86770440007/|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=hoopshype.com|language=en}} ==National team career== Quiñones plays for the [[Dominican Republic national basketball team|Dominican Republic national team]]. He joined the [[Dominican Republic men's national under-19 basketball team|under-18 team]] at the [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]] in [[St. Catharines|St. Catharines, Ontario]]. In six games, Quiñones averaged 17.5 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game, leading his team to sixth place.{{cite web|title=Lester Quinones (DOM)'s profile|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/americas/u18/2018/player/Lester-Quinones|work=[[FIBA]]|access-date=August 4, 2019}} His best performance came in a loss to [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rico]], in which he recorded 31 points and seven three-pointers.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=2019 guard Lester Quinones sees interest spike as he plays for Dominican U18 team|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/06/11/2019-guard-lester-quinones-sees-interest-spike-as-he-plays-for-dominican-u18-team/|website=ZagsBlog.com|date=June 11, 2018|access-date=August 4, 2019}} ==Personal life== Quiñones was born in the [[United States]], but is of Salvadoran, Dominican and Puerto Rican descent.{{Cite web | title=Golden State Warriors {{!}} NBA.com | url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/videos/lester-quinoness-latino-heritage | access-date=2025-02-15 | website=www.nba.com}} Internationally, he represents the [[Dominican Republic men's national basketball team|Dominican Republic]].{{cite web|first=Parth|last=Upadhyaya|title=Lester Quinoñes to play with Dominican National Team against Memphis|url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/37368/lester-quinones-dominican-national-basketball-team-memphis-tigers|website=DailyMemphian.com|date=July 18, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2024}}
